Step 3: minimal elements are squarefree; C = minimal transversals of supports. Wait: minimal elements of S_∞ correspond to minimal transversals? h ∈ S_∞ iff supp(h) is a transversal of {supp(a_i)}. Minimal under divisibility = minimal transversal under inclusion (squarefree). Yes.

Proof: (a) Zorn ok (chain: {e∩T_α} is chain of nonempty subsets of finite e, has smallest element... actually a chain under inclusion of finite nonempty sets has minimal element = intersection? Under reverse inclusion ordering, intersection of chain works since for each e, e∩(∩T_α) = min of chain {e∩T_α}, nonempty since chain of nonempty finite sets has minimal element contained in all. Yes.)

(b) Case A: F_s infinite; T ⊆ I∪Z_s ⊆ e for all e ∈ F_s; antichain forces e=T. Good.

Case B: r ∈ g_s\{t} in infinitely many F_s members — pigeonhole on finite g_s\{t}. F_{s+1} infinite. Also r ∉ Z_s: since z_i chosen: is z_{i+1} ∈ g_s for earlier? Actually need r ∉ Z_s. Claimed g_s ∩ Z_s = ∅ since g_s disjoint from I∪Z_s. Yes. Good.

(c): Every member meets I∪Z_ω. Suppose g disjoint. Then always eligible. "At stage s+1 the least eligible member g_s receives z_{s+1} ∈ g_s, so g_s ineligible later" — indeed g_s ∩ Z_ω ⊇ {z_{s+1}} ≠ ∅... wait eligibility means disjoint from I∪Z_s. Once z_{s+1} ∈ g_s, g_s is ineligible at stages > s+1. Fine. index(g_{s+1}) ≥ index(g_s): g_{s+1} eligible at stage s+1 means disjoint from I∪Z_{s+1}; at stage s+1 the least eligible chosen was g_s with Z_s; is g_{s+1} eligible at stage s+1's selection? g_{s+1} chosen at stage s+2, disjoint from I∪Z_{s+1} ⊇ I∪Z_s, so eligible at stage s+1, so index ≥ index(g_s). Also strictly: since g_{s+1} ≠ g_s and index monotone... actually index(g_{s+1}) ≥ index(g_s), and inequality: could be equal? g_{s+1} ≠ g_s so indices differ; since ≥, strictly increasing. Then unbounded. g eligible at all stages with fixed index < index(g_s) eventually — contradiction. Good.

Final: T finite ⊆ I∪Z_ω, choose s with T ⊆ I∪Z_s; F_{s+1} infinite contains e ≠ T with e ⊇ I∪Z_{s+1} ⊇ T, e ⊋ T (since e ∈ C_I, e∩t = I, e ≠ T... need e ⊋ T not e = T; e ≠ T and e ⊇ T so strict). Contradiction. Good.

One subtlety: Z_ω may not be a set but the argument works; also g ∈ C disjoint from I∪Z_ω: at stage s+1, if Case B, least-index eligible is g_s; if g eligible at stage s+1 then index(g) ≥ index(g_s) — that's the claim "index(g) ≥ index(g_s) for all s" — yes since g is eligible at every stage. Good.

Also Zorn's lemma use: fine (AC).

Also self-dual property (iii) used: minimal transversal is member. Correct.

So proof is complete and correct. Grade 7.
